content:
oncall-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected on /v1/generate — p95 latency jump to ~820ms, p99 ~2.4s, streaming stalls reported. paging oncall (severity: high) :rotating_light:

maya: I got paged. looking at dashboards now — streaming tail looks nasty. any known deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy finished 3m ago: service=inference-runtime image=redwood/runtime:1.48.3

maya: ok noted. sam/CS, any customer reports?

sam: a couple of customers reported stalled webstreams ~7–10m ago, one reported "no tokens for 10s" then resumed. collecting customer ids.

liam: checking KV cache metrics — kv.cache.evictions/s spiked at the same time as latency. prefill vs decode worker imbalance looks possible (prefill backlog).

maya: where are those metrics? query?

liam: Grafana panel: infra.kv.*. Sample prometheus: `sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (pool)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(prefill_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]))`

eva: dug into pod logs: prefill pods show increased backlog and OOM-kill attempts earlier. decode pods remained healthy but starved for KV entries -> small decode bursts then long stalls while waiting for prefill.

maya: so prefill <-> decode imbalance causing fragmentation and lots of evictions, leading to misses and decode stalls -> tail latency.

liam: immediate mitigations I propose:
1) throttle low-priority/async routes (reduce incoming pressure)
2) scale prefill pool + bump prefill worker concurrency for affected node pool
3) temporarily disable heavy-context streaming batching for hosted tier to reduce KV pressure
4) enable emergency cache-growth (increase kv_cache_max_entries) on affected clusters

maya: agree. I'll throttle via rate-limit rule on edge for 10m: `rlimit: host=hosted,route=/v1/stream,rate=50rps` then rip through scaling.

eva: scaling prefill now: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/prefill --replicas=10` (was 4). watching for steady state.

liam: making a rolling config change to increase kv cache capacity + eviction_grace to reduce churn. patch applied to canary in us-west: `kv_cache.max_entries=2e6` and `eviction_grace=15s`

maya: confirming: after throttling + scale, p95 dropped to ~190ms, p99 ~520ms. streaming stalls reduced.

sam: customers on support threads notified and given ETA 30m for full remediation. no data loss reported.

liam: root cause note so far: workload spike of many long-context streams + recent runtime image changed memory footprint causing prefill worker throughput to drop. combined with conservative cache bounds -> fragmentation and evictions. prefill couldn't keep up -> decode starved -> streaming stalls/tail latency.

maya: handing off to liam for long tail and post-incident actions. I'm going offline in 20m.

liam: taking over. next steps:
- stabilize: keep prefill scaling + cache bump for 1h
- rollback runtime image on canary if we see memory regression
- add alert on kv.prefill_queue_depth > 50 for 5m
- add eviction-rate alert tied to p99 latency to reduce blind spots
- postmortem doc + customer impact summary

maya: thanks. please ping if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

liam: will do. adding TODOs in incident tracker. will draft postmortem and action items: adjust prefill/decoder ratio tests and add synthetic streaming load to CI to catch this pattern.

oncall-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff recorded — previous: maya -> next: liam. escalation channel: #eng-sre.

liam: closing thread once metrics stable for 30m. current status: mitigations active, partial customer impact (stream delays), no ongoing pages.

maya: ack, thanks everyone.
